title: Minimum Platforms
statement:
A railway station timetable lists `n` trains. Train `i` arrives at time `arrival[i]` and departs at time `departure[i]`; both are integers and `arrival[i] ≤ departure[i]`.

While a train is in the station it occupies one platform for the whole closed interval `[arrival[i], departure[i]]`. Two trains cannot share a platform if their intervals overlap or even touch, so a train that arrives at exactly the moment another train departs still needs a different platform. No train may wait outside the station: every train must get a platform at its arrival time and keep it until it departs.

Find the **minimum number of platforms** the station needs to serve the whole timetable.
input_format:
The first line contains `n`.
The second line contains the `n` arrival times.
The third line contains the `n` departure times, in the same train order.
output_format: Print a single integer: the minimum number of platforms.

examples.explanation: The trains occupy [10,25], [20,35], [30,45], [25,28] and [40,50]. At time 25 the first, second and fourth trains are all present, so 3 platforms are needed, and no moment has 4 trains.
The first train leaves at time 5, exactly when the second arrives. Their intervals touch, so they cannot share a platform.

hints: The answer is the largest number of trains that are in the station at the same moment.
Sort arrival times and departure times separately. You do not need to keep track of which departure belongs to which train.
Walk through arrivals in order. Before counting a new arrival, release every platform whose departure is strictly earlier than this arrival, then update the maximum.
reference:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    arr = sorted(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    dep = sorted(map(int, data[1 + n:1 + 2 * n]))
    j = 0
    cur = best = 0
    for i in range(n):
        while dep[j] < arr[i]:
            j += 1
            cur -= 1
        cur += 1
        if cur > best:
            best = cur
    print(best)

main()

import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
arr = [int(x) for x in data[1:1 + n]]
dep = [int(x) for x in data[1 + n:1 + 2 * n]]
best = 0
for i in range(n):
    t = arr[i]
    c = sum(1 for j in range(n) if arr[j] <= t <= dep[j])
    best = max(best, c)
print(best)
